entities.name: Luis de Torres
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Luis de Torres was the interpreter for Christopher Columbus's first voyage to America, facilitating communication between the Spanish expedition and the indigenous peoples of the Caribbean.

Born in 1450, Luis de Torres was a skilled linguist and diplomat from Valencia, Spain, who joined Columbus's crew as a translator and mediator. His linguistic expertise enabled him to interpret and facilitate interactions between Columbus and the native populations, facilitating the exchange of goods, ideas, and cultures.

Torres's significance extends beyond his role as a translator, as he played a crucial part in shaping the early history of the Americas. His language skills and cultural knowledge helped to establish a bridge between the Old and New Worlds, laying the groundwork for the complex cultural exchange that would shape the course of history.

The legacy of Luis de Torres can be seen in the enduring impact of his work on the history of the Americas, the Caribbean, and beyond. His contributions to the field of translation and diplomacy continue to inspire scholars and historians today.

'For the benefit of all Christians, we must discover the new trade routes and establish a new trade with the Indians.' - Christopher Columbus
